what_this_is: The Workshop rows for gathering words from people into an ordinary list in tools/gather-words-from-people: ask, keep with consent, approve exactly as reviewed, and read back what may be shown.

payload.label: Ask people for their words
payload.job: Ask people, each after their own good word, to say in their own words how it went: the asked row to keep for each person for a case, and their draft
payload.description: For each person who may be asked, answers the asked row to keep in the list and the person's draft ({to, subject, body}) from the words the list's gathers.ask holds, with {name} filled in. Sends nothing and keeps nothing: the draft goes out through a sending tool the person chose, and the caller's AI keeps the `keep` rows in its store. A person is asked once for a case (the same person and case, found among the `rows` handed in, is skipped as already_asked), and only with `win`, a reference to the person's own positive word that made this the time to ask (otherwise skipped as no_win). The address is in the draft only, never in the row to keep. Returns asked ({row_id, person, draft}), skipped ({person, reason}) and keep.

list.description: The list's definition (the value of its list row): its `gathers` block says which fields hold what. Read it from a store and hand it in.

case.description: What the asking is about, such as an order or a course: one ask per person per case

id.description: Who the person is in the person's own records

address.description: Where the draft goes; kept out of the row

win.description: The reference to their own positive word, such as a message id or a record id

rows.description: The list's rows as [{ id, value }], read from a store and handed in. This tool reads and keeps no records.

output_schema.description: { asked: [{ row_id, person, draft }], skipped: [{ person, reason }], keep: [{ id, type, value, expected }] }

payload.label: Keep the words a person gave
payload.job: Work out the row that keeps the words a person gave in reply, with the consent they gave and the words that gave it, as a received row of the list
payload.description: Answers the row that keeps words with one of the consents the list declares and consent_note, the person's own words that gave it (or where they are). With row_id it fills the row that asked them (found among the `rows` handed in); without it, `who` is required and the words become their own row, the same words from the same person always the same row. The row is received and any approval is taken away, so changed words are reviewed again. A withdrawn row takes no more words. The same call again changes nothing. Nothing is written by this tool: `keep` holds the records the caller's AI keeps in its store, conditional on the row as handed in. Returns row_id, status, changed and keep.

list.description: The list's definition (the value of its list row): its `gathers` block says which fields hold what. Read it from a store and hand it in.

who.description: The speaker, when no row asked them

words.description: Their words, exactly as they gave them

consent.description: One of the list's consent ids

consent_note.description: Their own words that gave this consent, or where they are kept

rows.description: The list's rows as [{ id, value }], read from a store and handed in. This tool reads and keeps no records.

output_schema.description: { row_id, status, changed, keep: [{ id, type, value, expected }] }

payload.label: Approve words to show
payload.job: Work out the approval, decline or withdrawal of one row of words exactly as it was reviewed, so only approved words are ever shown
payload.description: decision approve needs reviewed_words equal to the words now in the row, a received row, and a consent that allows showing: then the row to keep is approved and pinned to the speaker, the words and the consent together. decline marks a received row declined. withdraw (the person took their consent back, or the owner took the words down) works on any row and stops it showing at once. The row is found among the `rows` handed in. Nothing is written by this tool: `keep` holds the records the caller's AI keeps in its store, conditional on the row as handed in, so a store refuses it when the row changed since. Returns row_id, status and keep.

list.description: The list's definition (the value of its list row): its `gathers` block says which fields hold what. Read it from a store and hand it in.

reviewed_words.description: The words exactly as the reviewer read them; required to approve

rows.description: The list's rows as [{ id, value }], read from a store and handed in. This tool reads and keeps no records.

output_schema.description: { row_id, status, keep: [{ id, type, value, expected }] }

payload.label: Read the words that may be shown
payload.job: Read the words of a list that may be shown on a page: approved, consented to be shown, and unchanged since approval, as items for a page's proof section
payload.description: Takes the list's rows and returns only those whose state is approved, whose consent allows showing and whose pin still matches the speaker, words and consent now in the row, as items {heading, body, row_id} that a sales page takes as a proof section's items (heading = the name as the consent says: whole, first name only, or the list's own anonymous heading). Every other row is counted in held_back by its reason (not_approved, changed_since_approved, consent_does_not_allow_showing) and never returned. limit keeps the first items. Returns items, shown, may_show_total and held_back.

list.description: The list's definition (the value of its list row): its `gathers` block says which fields hold what. Read it from a store and hand it in.

rows.description: The list's rows as [{ id, value }], read from a store and handed in. This tool reads and keeps no records.

output_schema.description: { items: [{ heading, body, row_id }], shown, may_show_total, held_back }
